text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 0.2% today to $367.19, extending a sharp two-week decline of 1.5% that has seen the stock lose nearly $48 from mid-November. The drop tracks a broader weakness in refining stocks tied to crude oil prices—US oil closed today at $89.53 per barrel, down significantly from levels that were higher earlier in November. Refineries are running at 95.7% capacity with gasoline and diesel inventories both ample, which limits upside pricing power for refined products when crude itself softens.

The geopolitical tensions between Iran and Saudi Arabia reported today could normally support oil prices, but the market has priced in limited near-term supply risk so far. Longer-term, the energy sector faces structural headwinds: AI and data centers are set to double their electricity draw by 2030 according to the IEA, potentially dampening oil demand growth, while permitting reform moving through Congress signals an acceleration of renewable energy deployment that could also pressure future fuel consumption.
